name: Bottega Pizzeria
hours: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Sunday, 5 to 9 p.m. Thursday to Saturday, 5 to 10 p.m. Closed Monday.
why: Good for groups, private events, a seasonal terrace, and a wine list heavy on organic Italian producers. It has no private room, but it is the best fit here for a large group.

name: Buvette Beaubien
hours: Monday to Thursday, 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. Friday, 11 a.m. to midnight. Saturday, 10 a.m. to midnight. Sunday, 10 a.m. to 11 p.m.
why: It has a private dining room for up to 40 people and takes reservations. The menu is a natural wine list with charcuterie, cheese, and composed dishes such as mushroom polenta. There is also a terrace.

name: Café Guerrero
hours: Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. Closed Saturday and Sunday.
why: Rotating lunch menu with vegetarian options. Weekday lunch only, so it works only if the group has a free weekday midday.

name: Caffè Italia
hours: Monday to Wednesday, 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. Thursday, 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Friday, 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. Saturday, 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Sunday, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.
why: A Little Italy landmark with 1950s decor, espresso drinks, and paninis. It is listed as good for groups, has a seasonal patio, and stays open late on weekends. Counter service, no online reservations.

name: Damas
hours: Monday to Friday, 5:30 to 10 p.m. (one listing, so confirm).
why: It has a private room for 15 to 30 guests. A Canada's 100 Best review praised its salads and vegetable-focused mezze and said vegetarians would be happy.

name: Dépanneur Le Pick Up
why: Google describes the sandwiches as gourmet and veg-friendly. It seats about 20 inside and 20 outside in summer. Daytime only, so it suits a lunch.

name: Épicerie Pumpui
hours: Daily, noon to 3:30 p.m. and 4:30 to 9 p.m.
why: Classic Thai dishes with a terrace in season. The room is small (about six tables) and waits are common. No online reservations, so call (514) 379-3024.

name: Estiatorio Milos
hours: Monday to Wednesday, 11:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. and 5:30 to 11 p.m.
why: It has a private room, a full bar, takes reservations, and is priced at $51 and up. The menu includes a meatless signature dish of fried zucchini and eggplant with saganaki cheese, plus vegetable-based Greek spreads on the sides list.

name: Graziella
hours: Tuesday to Saturday for dinner, 5:30 to 9:30 p.m.
why: Private rooms seat 10 and 20 (30 combined), and a larger room seats 80. Vegetarian dishes are available. A Tastet review says the tables are spaced well enough that you can talk without hearing your neighbours. Watch: The kitchen closes at 9:30 p.m., so it suits an early dinner.

name: Mon Petit Poulet
hours: Tuesday to Sunday, 5 to 9 p.m. Closed Monday.
why: Casual comfort food with a liquor license (beer and wine). Google offers a “Find a table” link. A 2018 review put seating at about 25, so it is best for a smaller group. Vegetarian options are not listed.

name: Pizza Bouquet
hours: Sunday to Thursday, noon to 9 p.m. Friday and Saturday, noon to 9:30 p.m.
why: Compact, no-frills counter spot selling slices or 16-inch pies. It is quick and cheap, but a poor fit for a seated group dinner.

name: Vin Mon Lapin
why: It is the closest option and a major name in the city. A vegetarian reviewer had dishes modified for her, and prices run $51 and up. Watch: It is best for small groups. OpenTable says parties of up to 6, while Tourisme Montréal lists private rooms for 12 to 20. The room is lively. Reservations open 30 days ahead, may be a concern for late reservations.

name: Alep
hours: Dinner only on Wednesday, 5 to 10:30 p.m. (also closed Monday).
why: Tasting menus can be adapted for vegetarian and vegan guests, and the wine list is strong. No private room.

name: Anemone
why: Groups of 10 or more get a shared 3 or 4 course menu at $80 per person. It takes private parties. The kitchen adapted dishes for a vegetarian reviewer, but another reviewer found the dining room very loud, so ask about the quietest seating.

name: Il Bazzali
hours: Sunday and Wednesday to Saturday, 5 to 10 p.m.
why: The largest private room holds 60. Vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options are listed. The chef is a tenor and sings at some dinners, so ask if your night will be quiet. Prices are listed from $31 to $65 depending on the source, so confirm it clears $50 with drinks.

name: Restaurant Limbo
why: Vegetables lead the menu, the wine list is natural, and the room suits quiet talk. Rated $$$$. I found no private room, and groups of 7 or more must call to book.
